summary: Reports an official IAB policy position on network management in the Internet, from the second ad hoc review group meeting on June 12, 1989. The results of the first such meeting appeared in RFC 1052.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reports an IAB review of Internet network-management work in 1989. It recommends giving SNMP and CMOT room to explore changes while maintaining opportunities to share management information.

questions: what is the difference between snmp and cmot
subtitle: The IAB's 1989 recommendations on SNMP, CMOT, and Internet management information.

tldr.problem: The earlier plan tied SNMP and CMOT to a common management information base, but the report says this appeared to limit exploration of new variables and functions.
tldr.mechanism: The review recommended independently exploring new variables and possibly separate SMI definitions for a period, while keeping non-shared variables in experimental or private MIB space.
tldr.outcome: The IAB approved the report and adopted its recommendations in July 1989. The document records a policy position at that time, not a protocol specification.

today: RFC 1109 is a policy report published in August 1989 and approved by the IAB in July 1989. Its metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: SNMP, CMOT, and the Common MIB
sections.content:
The earlier review selected SNMP and CMOT for further work and encouraged a common Management Information Base (MIB) and Structure of Management Information (SMI). The second review examined progress and whether the approach supported operational needs.

The report describes SNMP as having implementations and use in networks at that time. It reports no publicly available CMOT implementations at the meeting, although development was planned.
sections.plainLanguage: SNMP and CMOT were both under development, but their implementation experience differed. The review examined whether their shared management-information definitions were helping the work progress.

sections.title: Gaps in Network Management
sections.content:
The report lists areas not covered by the SNMP and CMOT specifications, including software downloading, configuration management, user access control, and authenticating management commands and responses.

It also describes open questions about correlating variables across network layers, identifying MIB versions, archiving operational data, and defining a general application programming interface. The report says that tying both protocols to one common MIB and SMI appeared to have impeded exploration of new variables and functions.
sections.plainLanguage: The management protocols did not cover every operational task, and the report identified several unanswered design questions. It also argued that requiring one shared information model could slow experimentation.

sections.title: Conclusions from the Review
sections.content:
The attendees concluded that the Internet would contain multiple protocol stacks and that coexistence would remain necessary. They also concluded that expansion of the common MIB had been impeded by difficulty agreeing on an extended SMI.

The report called for continued work on OSI management tools while meeting operational Internet needs. It said that a coexistence and transition plan could not be specified until there was operational experience with those tools.
sections.plainLanguage: The review expected several management approaches to coexist. It recommended gaining practical experience before deciding how to transition between them.

sections.title: Recommendations to the IAB
sections.content:
The report recommended allowing SNMP and CMOT efforts to explore new variables and potentially non-overlapping SMI definitions independently for the next 12 months. Variables not supported by both protocols could be defined in experimental or private MIB space.

It also recommended encouraging OSI-based elements, working with NIST on coexistence, restructuring IETF network-management work if needed, and reconvening the review group at six-month intervals.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB was asked to allow independent experimentation for a defined period and to keep reviewing whether common management definitions could expand. The report also called for coordination with NIST.
